newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SPC says 1996 profits up, margins under pressure.
newsitem.headline: SPC says 1996 profits up, margins under pressure.

text.p: Singapore Petroleum Co Ltd (SPC) said on Thursday it expected increasing competition in Asia to adversely affect refining margins.
The company said its net profit in calendar 1996 rose 1.5 percent to Singapore $26.91 million from a year before.
It attributed the improved performance to better product margins and the results from a full-year's operation of a residue catalytic cracker.
This helped more than double operating profits to $103 million, although the new unit meant depreciation charges more than doubled and interest expenses almost tripled.

"While the directors remain optimistic about longer term prospects, persistent and increasing competition from the regional refineries will continue to adversely impact on current refining margins," the company said in a statement.
"The regional economies are however expected to continue showing strong demand growth in energy consumption," it added.
Singapore refining margins based on Dubai crude oil are assessed at a profit of $1.80 per barrel for basic refining operations and at a profit of $5.25 for more sophisticated operations.

SPC has an equal share in Singapore Refining Co, a 285,000 barrels-per-day refinery off Singapore. Other shareholders are British Petroleum Co Ltd Plc and Caltex, itself a joint venture equally owned by Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp of the United States.
Many countries in Asia are experiencing double digit growth in energy consumption and Asia is expected to be the biggest regional consumer -- overtaking north America -- by the end of the decade.
